feature.summary: Topic choice, adding a topic and dismissing a topic are not built on any app. Picking sources is partly built: web and desktop schedule forms have source checkboxes (project, memory, web; recent chats on web only) and a connector list, which is 'coming soon'. The brief lists S42.03 as missing, so code and brief disagree.

purpose.what_it_does: Target: the person chooses what the briefing covers (topics) and which connected sources it reads, and can add or dismiss topics later. Today only per-schedule source switches exist on web and desktop, and the free-text prompt.
purpose.why_it_exists: Items S42.02, S42.03, S42.13 and S42.14 in the area brief (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/042-proactive-assistance-briefings-and-reflection.md). A briefing is more useful if it can be tuned without rewriting a prompt.
purpose.who_uses_it: People with a Daily briefing schedule who want a different focus.
problems_solved: Editing a long fixed prompt is hard for non-technical users.
Reading sources the person does not want is a privacy concern.
A topic that no longer matters keeps appearing.
use_cases: Turn off 'The web' for a private brief.
Exclude one connected mailbox from the brief.
Add 'competitor X' to the weekly brief.

where_to_find_it: Web: schedule create or edit form, section 'What Each Run Can Use' with 'Sources' and 'Connectors' (apps/web/features/schedules/components/ScheduleAccessFields.tsx:93).
Desktop (Tauri build): the same section from DesktopScheduleAccessFields (apps/desktop/src/features/schedules/DesktopScheduleAccessFields.tsx).
Mobile, CLI, VS Code: no source or topic control found (no 'sources' in apps/mobile/src/features/schedules).
Chrome: no checkbox control; the form sends the template's sources unchanged (schedulesSection.ts:672,773).
Topics, add topic, dismiss topic: not available anywhere.
prerequisites: A schedule being created or edited (web, desktop).
Connectors being released for the connector list to appear; it is 'coming soon' now (connector-release.ts:14).
screens_and_controls: Web checkboxes: 'Project instructions and files' (only with a project), 'Saved memories' (read only while memory is on), 'The web', 'Recent chats' (your chats from the last 24 hours, read only while Search past chats is on) (ScheduleAccessFields.tsx:29-52).
Web connectors: one checkbox per connected connector; unchecked list limits the run; 'Includes every connector, even ones you connect later. Uncheck to choose.' (ScheduleAccessFields.tsx:211).
Desktop: three source checkboxes (project, memory, web) with no Recent chats (DesktopScheduleAccessFields.tsx:33-38).
journey: Open a schedule form on web or desktop.
Save; the choice is stored on the schedule.
At run time the executor honours the flags.
Topic add or dismiss: no journey exists.
feedback_and_outputs: While connectors load: 'Reading your connectors…'; on error a message and 'Try again'; with none connected 'No connectors are connected.' and a 'Connect one' link.
settings: Settings > memory and 'Search past chats' decide whether those sources read anything (ScheduleAccessFields.tsx:41-52).

working: Sources object saved with the schedule and enforced at run time: project, memory, web, recentChats (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:926-1004).
Web source checkboxes and connector list (ScheduleAccessFields.tsx:93-215).
incomplete: Desktop omits 'Recent chats' although the Daily briefing template sets it on (DesktopScheduleAccessFields.tsx:33-38; schedules.ts:854).
Mobile and Chrome cannot change sources (no control found).
Monitor a topic template holds a placeholder the person must edit by hand: 'Track [replace this with the topic you want followed]...' (schedules.ts:858).
disconnected_or_disabled: Connector choices are replaced by 'Connectors for scheduled runs are coming soon.' (ScheduleAccessFields.tsx:136).
not_available: Topic picker, add topic, dismiss topic on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome (brief S42.02, S42.13, S42.14 missing; no code found).
Mail and calendar source toggles by name; only generic connectors exist.

established.statement: The user chooses the topics the briefing covers (S42.02).
The user picks which connected sources (mail, calendar, apps) the briefing reads (S42.03).
The user can dismiss a topic (S42.13) and add a topic (S42.14).

acceptance_criteria: Web form shows four source checkboxes and each saved value changes what the run reads.
With 'The web' unchecked, the run has no web search tool.
Desktop form offers the same four sources as web.
Mobile offers a way to see and change sources, or the brief documents it does not.
A topic added is included in the next brief; a dismissed topic is not.
Connector list lets the person exclude a connector from the run.
inferred: Topics could be stored as structured data rather than prompt text [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Store topics on the schedule and build the prompt from them.
[proposed] Add the Recent chats checkbox to desktop and a sources screen to mobile.
[proposed] Replace the Monitor a topic placeholder with a required topic field.

steps.what_happens: Person changes source checkboxes in the schedule form.
Save sends the sources and connectors with the schedule to the schedules API.
At run time the executor reads task.sources (default if absent), loads memory and recent chats only when allowed by account policy, and enables web only when sources.web is true.
If the run could reach Google data, the executor requires a route that keeps inputs out of training.

corrections.claim: Executor loads memory and recent chats only when allowed by account policy (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:926-1004)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: The policy gating is in resolveScheduledContext (about lines 405-500), not 926-1004. Recent chats are gated by memoryPolicy.searchPastChats; memory goes through managedMemoryContextLoader with the policy. The 926-1004 range only passes the flags.
corrections.correction: At run time the executor passes sources.memory and sources.recentChats into resolveScheduledContext (lines ~405-500), which applies the memory policy and the Search past chats setting; web is enabled only when sources.web is true (line 984).

corrections.claim: Save sends sources and connectors to the schedules API (apps/web/app/api/schedules/route.ts:96-139)
corrections.what_the_code_shows: POST create handler is there (lines 96-136) and passes the body to createSchedule, but route.ts exports only GET and POST. PUT/update lives under [id]/. Section 5 'POST and PUT /api/schedules ... route.ts' is wrong for PUT. The handler also applies rate limit, CSRF, plan quota, workspace feature gate.
corrections.correction: POST /api/schedules (route.ts) creates; updates go through apps/web/app/api/schedules/[id]/route.ts.

corrections.claim: Web form shows four source checkboxes each saved value changes what the run reads (acceptance 1) and defaults
corrections.what_the_code_shows: Project checkbox is hidden without a project, so often three show; default recentChats is false.
corrections.correction: Web shows four checkboxes only when the schedule has a project; otherwise three.

missing_facts: A schedule made from the Daily briefing template on mobile (and any update without sources) loses recentChats:true, because the mobile template drops sources and the default is recentChats:false: MANAGED_CLOUD_SCHEDULE_DEFAULT_SOURCES at packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:101-106; apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/templates.ts:26-42. The Daily briefing prompt (schedules.ts:~850) asks for recent chats, so the mobile briefing silently lacks that input.

The executor resolves context through the shared context engine with organization context policy (loadOrganizationContextPolicy) and per-source budgets, so workspace admin policy can also block memory or project sources, not only the user's settings: apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:405-432.
Web-search and tools are also limited by an attached agent's config (webSearch, allowed/blocked domains), so unchecking is not the only control: scheduled-agent-executor.ts:984-1000.
